record.paper_title: Some open problems about the solutions of the delay difference equation x_{n+1}=A/x_n^2+1/x_{n-k}^p
record.context_brief: Existence, stability, and basins for period-two cycles
record.original_question: Let A>0, p>0, and k be a nonnegative integer, and consider x_{n+1}=A/x_n^2+1/x_{n-k}^p for n=0,1,..., with arbitrary positive initial values x_{-k},...,x_0. For which conditions on A, p, and k does this recurrence have nonconstant positive periodic cycles of period two; under which of those conditions are the period-two cycles stable; and what are their basins of attraction?

evidence.quote: Eqs. (1) and (16) are special cases of the delay difference equation x n+1 = A/x 2 n + 1/x p n−k n= 0,1, . . . (19) where A, p ∈(0,∞) and k∈ {0,1, . . . }and the initial conditions x−k, . . . , x 0 are arbitrary positive numbers.

Open problem 2. ... (b) Obtain conditions on A,p and k under which Eq. (19) has periodic cycles of period two. Under what conditions on A,p and k are these periodic cycles stable? What is the basin of attraction?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix real parameters $A>0$ and $p>0$, and a nonnegative integer $k\in\{0,1,2,\dots\}$. Consider the delay difference equation
$$x_{n+1}=\frac{A}{x_n^{2}}+\frac{1}{x_{n-k}^{p}},\qquad n=0,1,2,\dots,$$
with arbitrary positive initial values $x_{-k},x_{-k+1},\dots,x_0>0$.

A positive sequence $(x_n)$ is called a (prime) period-two cycle if there exist positive numbers $\phi\ne\psi$ such that $x_n=\phi$ for even $n$ and $x_n=\psi$ for odd $n$ (or vice versa) for all sufficiently large $n$, and this pair solves the recurrence.

Solve the following three problems:
(a) Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on $(A,p,k)$ under which the recurrence admits a nonconstant positive periodic cycle of prime period two.
(b) Among the parameter triples in (a), determine those for which such a period-two cycle is (locally asymptotically) stable.
(c) For each stable period-two cycle, describe explicitly its basin of attraction in the positive cone $(0,\infty)^{k+1}$ of admissible initial data.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a paper that fully resolves the existence, stability, and basin-of-attraction questions for prime period-two cycles of this specific delay rational recurrence in the full parameter regime $(A,p,k)$. Related works treat similar families (e.g., $x_{n+1}=\alpha + x_{n-k}^p/x_n^q$, where period-two solutions exist iff $k$ is odd), but no source verifying a complete solution of this particular open problem was found.

status_evidence.title: Some Notes on the Difference Equation x_{n+1}=α+x_{n-1}/x_n^k
status_evidence.snippet: Studies prime-period-two solutions for related rational delay recurrences, with existence depending on parity of the delay.
status_evidence.claim: Related rational delay difference equations have been analyzed for period-two cycles, but not the exact equation in question.

status_evidence.title: On the recursive sequence x_{n+1}=x_{n-1}/g(x_n)
status_evidence.snippet: Analysis of periodic and stability behavior of similar nonlinear delay recurrences.
status_evidence.claim: No complete answer to existence/stability/basin questions for the given equation is provided.
